agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: EU Regulation 2024/900 harmonises transparency and due-diligence rules for political advertising. It requires labels and transparency notices on political ads, a European ad repository, and limits targeting using personal data. It restricts pre-election sponsorship to EU-linked sponsors and sets sanction maxima of 6% of turnover. Applies from 10 October 2025.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2024/900 sets harmonised EU rules on transparency and due diligence for political advertising services and sponsors, and on targeting and ad-delivery techniques that process personal data. Political advertising covers paid or in-house messages by, for or on behalf of political actors, or liable and designed to influence elections, referendums or legislative processes; official communication, editorial content and personal opinions are excluded. Publishers must label each political advertisement and publish a transparency notice, keep records for seven years, and very large platforms have extra repository duties and feed a public European repository. Personal-data targeting requires separate explicit consent; special-category profiling and targeting of persons known to be at least one year below voting age are prohibited. Controllers must adopt internal policies and annual risk assessments. In the three months before elections, services are limited to eligible sponsors. Non-EU providers need legal representatives. Member States set sanctions up to 6% of annual turnover or income. Applies from 10 October 2025.

notes: Text is the Official Journal version of 20.3.2024; no consolidated text was used. Application: Article 30(2) sets application from 10 October 2025, but Article 3 and Article 5(1) apply from entry into force (twentieth day after publication, Article 30(1)); the entry-into-force date itself is not stated in the text. Article 28(2) gives a delegation period running from 9 April 2024, a date not otherwise stated. Article 25(2) sets two alternative maximum bases, (a) 6 % of annual income or budget (whichever is highest) and (b) 6 % of worldwide turnover, without saying when each applies. Article 7(1) uses 'provider of advertising services', a term not defined here, where Article 3(6) defines 'provider of political advertising services'. ‘political advertising’ means the preparation, placement, promotion, publication, delivery or dissemination, by any means, of a message, normally provided for remuneration or through in-house activities or as part of a political advertising campaign:

definitions.defined_in: this Regulation, by reference to Article 57 TFEU

evidence.quote: ‘service’ means any self-employed economic activity, normally provided for remuneration, as referred to in Article 57 TFEU;
‘political advertisement’ means an instance of political advertising published, delivered or disseminated by any means;
‘political actor’ means any of the following:
a ‘political party’ as defined in Article 2, point 1, of Regulation (EU, Euratom) No 1141/2014
‘political advertising service’ means a service consisting of political advertising with the exception of an online ‘intermediary service’
an online ‘intermediary service’, as defined in Article 3, point (g), of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065
‘provider of political advertising services’ means a natural or legal person engaging in the provision of political advertising services, with the exception of purely ancillary services;
‘political advertising campaign’ means the preparation, placement, promotion, publication, delivery or dissemination of a series of linked political advertisements
‘very large online platform’ means an online platform designated as a very large online platform pursuant to Article 33(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065;
‘very large online search engine’ means an online search engine designated as a very large online search engine pursuant to Article 33(4) of Regulation (EU) 2022/2065;
‘sponsor’ means the natural or legal person at whose request or on whose behalf a political advertisement is prepared, placed, promoted, published, delivered or disseminated;

‘targeting techniques’ means techniques that are used to address a political advertisement only to a specific person or group of persons, or to exclude them, on the basis of the processing of personal data;
‘ad-delivery techniques’ means optimisation techniques that are used to increase the circulation, reach or visibility of a political advertisement
‘political advertising publisher’ means a provider of political advertising service that publishes, delivers or disseminates political advertising through any medium;

definitions.defined_in: Regulation (EU) 2016/679, Art. 4 point 7; Regulation (EU) 2018/1725, Art. 3 point 8

evidence.quote: ‘controller’ means a ‘controller’ as defined in Article 4, point 7, of Regulation (EU) 2016/679 or, where applicable, as defined in Article 3, point 8, of Regulation (EU) 2018/1725.
a ‘European political party’ as defined in Article 2, point 3, of Regulation (EU, Euratom) No 1141/2014
‘profiling’ as defined in Article 4, point 4, of Regulation (EU) 2016/679

obligations.conditional_on: where applicable (Art. 11(1)(c) and (d))

obligations.summary: Political advertising publishers shall ensure that the transparency notice includes the Art. 12(1) items (a) to (m), including sponsor identity, remuneration, period, aggregated amounts and value of benefits, methodology, links and reach/engagement data where applicable. Under Art. 12(3) notices shall be in each advertisement or easily retrievable, kept up to date, machine-readable when made available electronically, in the language of the advertisement, accessible and clearly visible.
obligations.conditional_on: where applicable (Art. 12(1)(k) to (m))

evidence.quote: Political advertising publishers shall ensure that the transparency notice referred to in Article 11(1), point (e), includes the following information:

evidence.quote: Where the information cannot be completed or corrected without undue delay, the political advertising publisher shall not make the political advertisement available

evidence.quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 28 to amend this Regulation

evidence.quote: By 10 July 2025, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts to establish the format of and provide technical specifications for the transparency notice

evidence.quote: Political advertising publishers that are very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall ensure that each political advertisement

evidence.quote: they shall continue to provide access to the information required by Article 12(1) of this Regulation for the period referred to in Article 9(3)

evidence.quote: shall make each such political advertisement and the information required under Article 12(1) available in the European repository no later than 72 hours after the first publication

evidence.quote: By 10 April 2026, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts in accordance with Article 29 to set out detailed arrangements

obligations.summary: Political advertising publishers shall include in their management report, under Art. 19 of Directive 2013/34/EU, information on amounts or value of benefits received for services, including use of targeting and ad-delivery techniques, aggregated by campaign, and make it available to competent authorities where established under national law.

evidence.quote: Political advertising publishers shall include information on the amounts or the value of other benefits received in part or full exchange for the services provided

obligations.summary: Political advertising publishers shall have free, easy-to-access mechanisms for natural or legal persons to notify non-compliant advertisements, accepting electronic notifications where possible and containing the Art. 15(3) elements; they shall send confirmation of receipt without undue delay, provide redress information and information on automated means, and (non-VLOP publishers) make best efforts to examine notifications and inform notifiers on request.

evidence.quote: Political advertising publishers shall have in place the necessary mechanisms to enable natural or legal persons to notify them

evidence.quote: Political advertising publishers which are very large online platforms and very large online search engines shall without undue delay:

evidence.quote: In the last month preceding an election or a referendum, political advertising publishers shall process any notification they receive about a political advertisement linked to that election or referendum within 48 hours

obligations.conditional_on: upon a request by a national competent authority

evidence.quote: The transmitted information shall be complete, accurate and trustworthy

obligations.summary: At the request of interested entities (vetted researchers, civil society organisations, political actors, electoral observers, journalists), providers of political advertising services shall transmit promptly and free of charge the information required under Arts. 9, 11 and 12, in machine-readable form where possible, within one month or with a reasoned response; they may aggregate or range amounts to protect commercial interests, may refuse manifestly unclear or excessive requests, and may charge a reasonable fee for significant costs.
obligations.conditional_on: at the request of interested entities

evidence.quote: providers of political advertising services shall transmit promptly and free of charge, and where technically possible in a machine-readable format

evidence.quote: targeting techniques or ad-delivery techniques that involve the processing of the personal data of a data subject

obligations.conditional_on: use of targeting or ad-delivery techniques involving processing of personal data

evidence.quote: Member States shall designate one national competent authority responsible for keeping publicly available and machine-readable online registers

obligations.summary: Member States shall designate competent authorities for Arts. 18 and 19 (data protection supervisory authorities), for intermediary service providers under Arts. 7 to 17 and 21 (with Digital Services Coordinators coordinating), and one or more independent authorities for other aspects; they shall provide resources and national cooperation, and designate a national contact point. evidence.quote: Each Member State shall designate one or more competent authorities to be responsible for the application and enforcement of the aspects of this Regulation

evidence.quote: Member States shall report annually to the Commission on the sanctions imposed to enforce the provisions of this Regulation

evidence.quote: Member States shall publish the dates of their elections and referendums and, where applicable, of their electoral periods

evidence.quote: The power to adopt delegated acts referred to in Article 12(6) and Article 19(5) shall be conferred on the Commission for a period of four years from the 9 April 2024.
